DA: An alliance in tatters

By: Joy Summers | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The election of Helen Zille to the DA federal chair has led to a raft of resignations, exposed the cracks in the alliance and put the party in a tailspin. Can it ever recover

Unique Selling Point:
INTERVIEW WITH SOME OF THE KEY ROLE PLAYERS AS THE STORY UNFOLDS - INCLUDING DA FED CHAIR PERSON HELEN ZILLE

Summary:
WE LOOK AT THE RECENT EVENTS INSIDE THE DA SINCE FORMER LEADER MMUSI MAIMANE CALLED FOR AN INDEPENDENT REVIEW PANEL REPORT ON WHY THE DA HAD DONE BADLY AT THE ELECTIONS. THE REPORT HE COMMISSIONED SUGGESTED THAT MMAIMANE LEADERSHIP HAD NOT TAKEN THE DA FORWARD AND RECOMMENDED HE STEP DOWN. AS PART OF THE REVIEW PANEL INTROSPECTION THE DA ELECTED HELEN ZILLE AS THEIR FEDERAL CHAIR. THAT WAS A LINE IN THE SAND FOR JOHANNESBURG MAYOR HERMANN MASHABA WHO ANNOUNCED HIS RESIGNATION ON MONDAY. ON TUESDAY FURTHER RESIGNATIONS FOLLOWED - MMUSI MAIMANE AND ATHOL TROLIPPE RESIGNED. NOW THE DA IS LEADERLESS AND ACCUSED OF GOING BACKWARDS. WE FOLLOW THIS UNFOLDING NEWS STORY AND PUT HELEN ZILLE IN THE HOT SEAT AND ASK SOLLY MSIMANGA HOW HE SEES NOT ONLT THE FUTURE OF THE DA BUT THE FUTURE OF JOHANNESBURG AND BLACK PEOPLE WITHIN THE PARTY

Script:


DA IN TURMOIL FINAL SCRIPT TX SUNDAY 3rD NOVEMBER 2019 FACT CHECKED

Commentary One
Mmusi Maimane, once the protégé of Helen Zille, was riding the blue wave in 2016. Under his leadership the DA removed the ANC from three important Metro’s

Mmusi
People voted for change and now we must look to 2019

Commentary Two
Three years later, it’s all come crashing down.

Th 2019 elections saw the DA lose 470 000 voters, official opposition status in two provinces, and fail to attract black voters in their numbers. So Maimane commissioned a panel to review what went wrong.

It was compiled by Ryan Coetzee, Tony Leon and Michiel Le Roux. It found many problems but the single most important factor was the failure of effective leadership. Refiloe Nt’sekhe is DA National spokesperson

Refiloe Nt’sekhe
When he commissioned the review there were very, very difficult recommendations made by the panel to say Mr. Maimane should step down

Commentary three
The review included others in the DA leadership too.

LINK
That opened up the important position of Federal chair – a DA equivalent similar to the ANC secretary general position. At the last- minute Helen Zille stepped out of retirement, threw her hat in the ring and was duly elected.

Commentary Four
24 hours later the DA’s mayor of Johannesburg Herman Mashaba resigned.

Herman
I cannot reconcile myself with a group of people who believe that race is irrelevant in the discussion of inequality and poverty in South Africa in 2019.

Commentary Five
Mashaba suggested Zille was favoured by right-wing elements, but she believes, there are other reasons for his resignation.

Masa
Where you shocked that he said that about you?
Helen
I was very puzzled and I have had a nice little WhatsApp conversation about it, with him subsequently, but go and ask Herman why he said that.

Commentary Six
But Mashaba told me he is not doing any interviews for now

Helen
He was worried but I know that there are other things going down, that I was going to break up the governing arrangement between the DA and the EFF – I don’t have the power to do that in this position. He also misunderstood that the review report was saying that that governing arrangement had to be broken up. It never said that at all! So that is what he was scared of.
Masa
Do you think there was more to his resignation?
Helen
I do think so but you will have to ask him

Commentary seven
And if Mashaba was unhappy, says Refiloe Nt’sekhe, he had access to a range of internal processes to deal with his unhappiness

Refiloe Nt’sekhe
so to speak out when you have never exhausted the party processes that are available to you to deal with these issues, it’s also concerning for me

Commentary Eight
But whatever Mashaba’s reasons, the optics for the DA aren’t good, and validated what their own review had already flagged; that the party is uncertain and divided on how to approach the question of race

Masa Kekana
Refiloe are black people in the DA just a front?
Refiloe Nt’sekhe
I am not a front! And if anyone wants to call me a front then it’s an insult I actually believe I am quite competent at what I am doing
Masa
Then what about people that say we want a party that says we acknowledge your pain, black people?
Refiloe
Those are the issues we will deal with and debate at congress because those are the very issues where we have had policy incoherence coming through and it’s important that the DA be given the space to go through that policy conference

LINK
But more was to come, much more. On the 22nd of October Mmusi Maimane called a press conference here at DA Head- quarters in Johannesburg, and it was clear to journalists something big was about to happen

Commentary nine
After a five- hour delay, he told the media he had been under attack from a few in the DA

Mmusi
There comes a time when a leader must step back from all noise and conjecture and make a sober and honest assessment of what the future does hold and I have done that with my wife and in the end we have come to the conclusion that despite my best efforts- perhaps the DA is not the best vehicle that is suited to take forward the vision of building one South Africa

Masa Kekana
You and Mmusi had a very close relationship at some point did you try and convince him to stay
Helen Zille
Yes I did! I absolutely tried to convince him to stay, but he didn’t resign from the DA, he only wanted to resign from the leadership and stay on as the parliamentary leader, but when he attacked the DA in that prepared speech- that became impossible
Masa Kekana
Did the DA see it as an attack?
Helen Zille
Well if you are going to say that the party you have led is not a one SA for all when you have just spent an entire election campaign convincing people that it is, that is a full- on attack and I don’t really think he believes that, and I said why did you say that? And he said: “well I had to give a convincing reason why I was going” and I said well the review report is the reason. That is the reason.

Commentary ten
Mmaimane has not been available to respond to Zille’s statement. Refiloe Nt’sekhe was also perplexed by the attack

Refiloe
That is a sad statement to make considering he was at the helm of the organisation. So how he makes that determination when the decision to go forward wasn’t even done by congress that is a sad day.

Commentary eleven
Then yet another resignation, this time from former Nelson Mandela Bay mayor, and chairman of the party, Athol Trollip.
Athol
The less than spectacular result must be part of my responsibility so I accept that when the buck stops at the leadership I was in one of those doors/ I realized this weekend was it was my time to go

Commentary Twelve
Social media and analysts went into overdrive. The DA was done for they said, and the return of a divisive Helen Zille was largely to blame

Helen
If people want to misquote me and misunderstand me I am so used it by now I literally shrug it off
Masa
Zillenator, wrecking ball do these names bother you at all?
Helen
No why should they? You missed out Godzilla didn’t you?
Masa
Are you a wrecking ball?
Helen
I am here not to wreck anything but to fix things and the majority of the leaders represented in the federal council thought that I was the best person to do that

Commentary Thirteen
But Zille will need circumspection. Her tweets on colonialism were flagged by the review panel as damaging to the DA brand. Political Analyst Ebrahim Fakir

Ebrahim Fakir
She may be there to fix the problem but Helen Zille can be a wrecking ball at the worst of times but the evidence of her leadership shows that under her watch the party grew fairly significantly

Commentary Fourteen
The matter of redress is hotly contested. Zille believes the best form of redress is to grow the economy, and she uses Singapore as an example, again.

Helen
If we say we have had a very discriminatory past which is true then we have to say what is the best formula for redress and that is what impressed me about Singapore, because within two generations -forty years from a base much poorer than Zimbabwe they have taken their people out of poverty. There redress has been spectacular and the question I ask myself, is how did they do that?
Masa
The commentary that is running out there is that this is the beginning of the end and…
Helen Laughs
Masa
..And one response from the Daily Maverick is that the DA is stumbling into the past and I actually want to read this quote from Richard Poplak. He says…
Helen
Richard Poplak is a rather contrived writer and a useless analyst! He clearly hasn’t seen what the party has been through in the past. This isn’t a crisis, this is the proof that the party is honest enough to hold its leaders to account – no other party does that
Masa
I am going to quickly read this to you. The DA is proof that culturally and racially South Africa has not progressed much at all that black and white South Africans are separated by a gulf so wide that it appears forever unbridgeable. Helen Zille has chosen to embody this divide
Helen
If you had to compare what Richard Poplak has done for democracy in South Africa compared to what many people have done including myself, it would pale into insignificance.
I mean Poplak who is Poplak? What kind of analytical background has he got!

Commentary Fifteen
Now a difficult journey lies ahead for the DA as they chart a new course at their Congress next April. And who can lead them out of their current morass? This week John Steenhuisen became the interim parliamentary leader, and along with Bonginkosi Madikizela and Makashule Gana they’ve put their names into the hat for the interim leader of the DA. Elections take place on 17th November.

Masa
DO you think the DA will be able to gain trust of black voters?
Ebrahim Fakir
It’s possible, but I think the DA will be interested in stabilizing and then reach out …

Commentary Sixteen
The DA says their date with destiny will be the local government elections in 2021. But will they still be around to make the date?

Ebrahim
I don’t think it’s the end, these processes will play themselves out through conflict and so on, so there will be a period in which they will be smaller, they may be more coherent and they will have to build from there but I am not sure they will disappear because remember quite apart from the people writing the DA obituary now, previously in every election what would be said is that the DA has now reached its ceiling and every election save for 2019, they confounded the skeptics and did better than every- one said they would

THE END

PROMO ONE
Helen Zille is back in the DA, Herman Mashaba, Mmusi Maimane and Athol Trollip are out
Masa
Zillenator, wrecking ball do these names bother you at all?
Helen
No why should they? You missed out Godzilla didn’t you?

PROMO TWO
Mmusi Maimane has left the DA and Athol Trollip’s resigned. Now John Steenhuisen, Bonginkosi Madikizela and Makashule Gana are competing for the interim leadership position

PROMO THREE
Does Helen Zille’s return to the DA signal a return to the past?
Masa: Refiloe are black people in the DA just a front?
Refiloe: I am not a front! And if anyone wants to call me a front then it’s an insult
